frank_support: Customer acct-acme-42 reported ~20% of streaming requests show up as 5xx in billing/logs but their client closed the stream first. They provided a few traces, attaching one below. Can oncall/eng take a look? :thinking_face:

lina_oncall: Ack. Can you paste the request_id and a raw trace? Also which SDK/version and region?

frank_support: request_id r-11f2a4b0, sdk-js v2.4.1, region us-west-2. Raw server debug snippet: 
```
[2026-03-16T18:12:40.123Z] accept conn from 10.12.3.45:52432 -> assigned worker-7
[2026-03-16T18:12:40.210Z] request r-11f2a4b0 start, model redwood-medium
[2026-03-16T18:12:41.005Z] response chunk sent (prefix) size=128
[2026-03-16T18:12:41.008Z] write to upstream failed: broken pipe (EPIPE)
[2026-03-16T18:12:41.009Z] gateway: marking request r-11f2a4b0 as 5xx for accounting
[2026-03-16T18:12:41.010Z] conn from 10.12.3.45 closed (FIN seen)
```
Note that FIN is observed after the broken pipe, but customer insists their client closed cleanly first. They say their extension sends graceful halfclose.

sasha_custsuccess: Customer provided a minimal repro using curl from their environment: 
```bash
curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=redwood-medium" \n  --data-binary $'\n{"prompt":"hello","stream":true}\n'
# They then ctrl-c after receiving first chunk
```
They claim billing shows a 5xx for these runs.

devon_sre: This looks like the classic midstream race where proxy write fails because peer already half-closed and kernel returns EPIPE on subsequent write. Current accounting rule: any upstream write error -> count as 5xx. That rule may be overbroad for chunked streaming where client-initiated halfclose should be considered a user abort, not gateway failure.

lina_oncall: Can we confirm where the EPIPE originates (edge proxy vs worker)? Any tcpdump or socket state logs? Also need sample of request/response headers captured.

frank_support: Customer captured the client-side socket state: they see a FIN→ACK sequence before any error locally. But our server logs show EPIPE first. Here are relevant headers they sent and our logged response headers: 
```
Client->Edge headers:
  Host: api.redwood.com
  Connection: keep-alive
  Transfer-Encoding: chunked
  Accept: text/event-stream

Edge->Client first chunk headers:
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  Content-Type: text/event-stream
  Transfer-Encoding: chunked
  Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 18:12:41 GMT
```

maya_engineer: Hypothesis: the TCP FIN arrives at edge, but due to our internal worker write buffering the first attempted write that triggers EPIPE happens before the FIN is fully processed in our write path, so our code sees EPIPE then logs 5xx. Two potential fixes: 1) change accounting heuristic to classify EPIPE as user-abort if a FIN was observed within a small window (e.g., 50ms) of the write error; 2) add a short graceful window where EPIPE triggers a soft-abort path instead of 5xx, and surface separate metric (user_abort_after_write).

devon_sre: I like (1) as a short-term mitigation. We'll need to ensure we have reliable FIN/close timestamps from the edge. Do we currently log socket teardown timestamps with sub-ms resolution? If not we should add them.

opsbot: Deploy incident flag created: INC-2026-328 streaming-epipe-rate. Priority set to P2. Owner unassigned.

lina_oncall: Pushing to P1 for billing impact. frank, can you collect a few more r-ids and the full worker logs (stack traces at time of EPIPE)? Also please pull a 30s tcpdump of a repro run (pcap) from a test host if customer consents.

frank_support: Will do. Captured three more request ids: r-11f2a4b0, r-11f2a4d5, r-11f2a4f2. I'll upload logs + pcap to the incident ticket. Customer says they can repro in their environment with ~10% frequency when they rapidly half-close.

maya_engineer: If we go the heuristic route, we'll need to: 
- correlate write error time with conn-close time in edge logs
- update metric pipeline to split "5xx_write_failure" into "5xx_server_error" vs "user_closed_midstream"
- ensure billing pipeline uses the new classification

sasha_custsuccess: Noted. I'll inform customer of temporary workaround: have them wait ~200ms after receiving the final chunk before client halfclose to avoid the race (not ideal, but reduces hits). Will also ask them for permission to run active repro from our test runner against their network conditions.

devon_sre: Action items: 
- frank: upload logs/pcap to INC-2026-328 (ETA 2h)
- maya: prototype heuristic change and unit tests (ETA 1d)
- devon: add socket teardown timestamps to edge logs (ETA 2d)
- lina: escalate billing pipeline to hold on retroactive charges until classification patched

lina_oncall: tagging eng-runtime and billing. @maya_engineer please take ownership of the engineering fix. I'll update status to P1.

maya_engineer: Taking ownership. I'll open a PR for the heuristic and a small metrics migration plan. For audit, we'll emit a new tag `stream_client_abort` so we can backfill counts.

frank_support: Uploaded traces and pcap to the incident ticket. Customer is on standby for us to run a repro if needed. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

opsbot: INC-2026-328 updated: owner=maya_engineer, priority=P1, labels=[streaming, billing, epipe]
